## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekaputtaka Sutta* (Ud 2.7; PTS Ud 14) is the seventh sutta of the second chapter of the *Udāna*. The text concerns the theme of grief and sorrow arising from attachment to those who are dear.

 In addition, computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 77 matching passages shared with 17 Pali texts, as well as automatic alignments with the Chinese *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125.6) and *Madhyamāgama* (T 26.60) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the opening narrative framework (§1.1–1.3) exhibits an almost verbatim correspondence (similarity 0.96) with the *Piyajātika Sutta* (MN 87), which likewise concerns the grief over a deceased only son [DharmaNexus]. Other segments of the sutta (§2.1–2.2) share conventional formulaic material with several Nikāya collections (such as AN 4, AN 10, SN 55, Kd 17, and Kd 6) and other discourses in the *Udāna*, notably the *Visākhā Sutta* (Ud 8.8) and the *Bāhiya Sutta* (Ud 1.10) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
